med.surgx.ilox-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.ilox-step-02.caption: A cancer operation is one part of a treatment plan agreed by a multidisciplinary team.

med.surgx.ilox-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.ilox-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.ilox-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.ilox-step-05.caption: Abdominal phase: supine with reverse Trendelenburg (open or laparoscopic).

med.surgx.ilox-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.ilox-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.ilox-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.ilox-step-07.caption: The midline is fast, bloodless and extensible in both directions, which is exactly what an unknown pathology needs.

med.surgx.ilox-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.ilox-step-08.caption: The purpose of a laparotomy is to find out.

med.surgx.ilox-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.ilox-step-09.caption: Peritoneal or liver metastases missed by staging, or a tumour fixed to structures that cannot be resected, mean a major resection will add risk without curing the patient.

med.surgx.ilox-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.ilox-step-10.caption: The stomach will replace the oesophagus, and it survives on a single vascular arcade along its greater curve.

med.surgx.ilox-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.ilox-step-11.caption: The left gastric artery carries the main lymphatic drainage of the lesser curve and the distal oesophagus.

med.surgx.ilox-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.ilox-step-13.caption: Burst abdomen and incisional hernia are closure failures, and closure technique is one of the few variables entirely under the surgeon's control.

med.surgx.ilox-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.ilox-step-14.caption: The mid and lower thoracic oesophagus is best reached from the right, where the aorta is not in the way.

med.surgx.ilox-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.ilox-step-18.caption: Margin status and nodal yield are reported by the pathologist, but only from a specimen they can orient.

med.surgx.ilox-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.ilox-step-20.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.ilox-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.ilox-step-21.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.ilox-step-22.title: Step 22
med.surgx.ilox-step-22.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.utx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.utx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.utx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.utx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.utx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.utx-step-05.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.utx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.utx-step-06.caption: Every endoscopic bladder operation starts with a complete map.

med.surgx.utx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.utx-step-08.caption: The choice of energy and irrigation fluid decides whether a patient can develop TUR syndrome, and an under-calibrated urethra is where post-operative strictures come from.

med.surgx.utx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.utx-step-09.caption: Removing the bulk first exposes the base and the stalk, and gives the pathologist the grade.

med.surgx.utx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.utx-step-10.caption: Stage depends on whether the tumour invades the detrusor.

med.surgx.utx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.utx-step-11.caption: Retained chips block the catheter and cause clot retention in recovery, and every chip is tissue the pathologist needs for staging or for an incidental cancer.

med.surgx.utx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.utx-step-13.caption: A perforation recognised in theatre changes the plan and is usually manageable; one recognised in recovery presents as abdominal distension, pain and fluid overload, and costs time the patient may not have.

med.surgx.utx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.utx-step-14.caption: After a resection the bladder must stay empty and free of clot while the raw surface stops oozing.

med.surgx.utx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.utx-step-15.caption: A single early instillation reduces recurrence in appropriately selected tumours, but in a perforated or bleeding bladder it can cause serious extravesical toxicity.

med.surgx.utx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.utx-step-16.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.utx-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.utx-step-18.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.usex-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.usex-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.usex-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.usex-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.usex-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.usex-step-04.caption: Supine with the legs slightly abducted; the penis taped up onto the abdomen.

med.surgx.usex-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.usex-step-05.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.usex-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.usex-step-06.caption: A midline raphe incision reaches both testes through one wound, which matters because both sides will be fixed.

med.surgx.usex-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.usex-step-07.caption: Restoring flow is the whole purpose of the operation.

med.surgx.usex-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.usex-step-08.caption: A testis that looks black on delivery often recovers colour after detorsion.

med.surgx.usex-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.usex-step-09.caption: A dead testis left in place risks infection and prolonged pain.

med.surgx.usex-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.usex-step-10.caption: The bell-clapper anatomy that allowed the torsion is still there after detorsion.

med.surgx.usex-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.usex-step-13.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.usex-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.usex-step-15.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.usex-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.usex-step-16.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.uscx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.uscx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.uscx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.uscx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.uscx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.uscx-step-04.caption: Supine, with slight head-down tilt to move bowel away from the bladder; lithotomy if cystoscopic guidance is used.

med.surgx.uscx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.uscx-step-05.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.uscx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.uscx-step-06.caption: Every endoscopic bladder operation starts with a complete map.

med.surgx.uscx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.uscx-step-07.caption: Bowel injury is the complication that kills after suprapubic catheterisation, and ultrasound is the cheapest way to prevent it.

med.surgx.uscx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.uscx-step-08.caption: Aspirating urine confirms the track and depth before the large trocar goes in.

med.surgx.uscx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.uscx-step-09.caption: The track has been proven; the risk now is depth.

med.surgx.parathyroide-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.parathyroide-step-09.caption: Monitoring only helps if you know it worked at the start.

med.surgx.parathyroide-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.parathyroide-step-10.caption: A focused operation is safe only when it goes exactly where the concordant imaging points.

med.surgx.parathyroide-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.parathyroide-step-11.caption: Seeing the recurrent laryngeal nerve along its course is the main defence against injuring it.

med.surgx.parathyroide-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.parathyroide-step-13.caption: A ruptured adenoma can seed parathyroid tissue through the neck and cause persistent or recurrent hyperparathyroidism that is very hard to cure.

med.surgx.parathyroide-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.parathyroide-step-14.caption: PTH has a short half-life, so removing the only hyperfunctioning gland produces a fall within minutes.

med.surgx.parathyroide-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.parathyroide-step-15.caption: When the localised gland is not found, or PTH does not fall, the patient is not cured.

med.surgx.parathyroide-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.parathyroide-step-16.caption: A signal recorded after the dissection tells you whether the nerve still conducts.

med.surgx.parathyroide-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.parathyroide-step-18.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.parathyroide-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.parathyroide-step-20.caption: Blood trapped deep to tightly closed strap muscles compresses the trachea and causes laryngeal venous congestion.

med.surgx.parathyroide-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.parathyroide-step-21.caption: A neck haematoma can obstruct the airway within minutes, and the people who see it first are recovery and ward staff, not the surgeon.

med.surgx.parathyroide-step-22.title: Step 22
med.surgx.parathyroide-step-22.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.lax-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.lax-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.lax-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.lax-step-02.caption: Endocrine operations treat a biochemical disease.

med.surgx.lax-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.lax-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.lax-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.lax-step-05.caption: Lateral decubitus with the operated side up, the table flexed at the level of the umbilicus or a kidney bridge raised to open the space between the costal margin and the iliac crest.

med.surgx.lax-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.lax-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.lax-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.lax-step-07.caption: Access is where laparoscopy injures people.

med.surgx.lax-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.lax-step-08.caption: Ports placed for the anatomy you have, rather than for the textbook, are the difference between a comfortable operation and a fight.

med.surgx.lax-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.lax-step-09.caption: The first look answers a question the imaging could not, and it is the only chance to find the second diagnosis before attention narrows to the first.

med.surgx.lax-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.lax-step-10.caption: Laparoscopic adrenalectomy is safe when gravity and mobilisation display the gland and its vein.

med.surgx.lax-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.lax-step-11.caption: Tumour cells shed into the wound, the peritoneum or a port site produce a recurrence that no adjuvant therapy fully reverses.

med.surgx.lax-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.lax-step-12.caption: The adrenal vein is the one structure in this operation that bleeds dangerously: on the right it is short and enters the vena cava directly, on the left it joins the renal vein.

med.surgx.lax-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.lax-step-13.caption: The adrenal is friable and its tumours may be malignant or hormonally active.

med.surgx.lax-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.lax-step-14.caption: Conversion is a safety manoeuvre, not a failure.

med.surgx.lax-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.lax-step-15.caption: Bringing an infected or neoplastic specimen through the abdominal wall unprotected causes port-site infection and, in malignancy, port-site recurrence.

med.surgx.lax-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.lax-step-17.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.lax-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.lax-step-19.caption: A port-site hernia through an unclosed 10 mm fascial defect can strangulate, and it presents days later to someone who was not in theatre.

med.surgx.lax-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.lax-step-20.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.lax-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.lax-step-21.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.lsx-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.lsx-step-18.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.lsx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.lsx-step-19.caption: A rhesus-negative woman exposed to fetal red cells can become sensitised, which threatens every future pregnancy.

med.surgx.lsx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.lsx-step-20.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.locx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.locx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.locx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.locx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.locx-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.locx-step-03.caption: Gynaecological and obstetric operations rest on a scan, a test result and a plan agreed in clinic.

med.surgx.locx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.locx-step-05.caption: Modified lithotomy (Lloyd-Davies) with legs in supports, arms tucked, and secured for steep head-down tilt.

med.surgx.locx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.locx-step-06.caption: The size, position and mobility of the uterus and the state of the cervix under anaesthesia decide the direction of every instrument that follows.

med.surgx.locx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.locx-step-07.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.locx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.locx-step-09.caption: Ports placed for the anatomy you have, rather than for the textbook, are the difference between a comfortable operation and a fight.

med.surgx.locx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.locx-step-10.caption: The first look answers a question the imaging could not, and it is the only chance to find the second diagnosis before attention narrows to the first.

med.surgx.locx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.locx-step-11.caption: The state of the remaining tube and both ovaries determines future fertility, the choice between salpingectomy and salpingotomy, and what the woman is told afterwards.

med.surgx.locx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.locx-step-12.caption: Rupturing an early ovarian cancer upstages it and can change treatment.

med.surgx.locx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.locx-step-13.caption: The ureter crosses the pelvic brim beside the infundibulopelvic ligament and passes beneath the uterine artery close to the side of the cervix.

med.surgx.locx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.locx-step-14.caption: The right incision, on the antimesenteric side and just through the thin cortex, finds the cleavage plane without entering the cyst and keeps away from the hilar vessels.

med.surgx.locx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.locx-step-15.caption: Removing the cyst intact in its plane preserves as much cortex as possible and avoids spillage.

med.surgx.locx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.locx-step-16.caption: The ovarian bed oozes, and the instinct to coagulate it widely destroys the follicles the operation was meant to preserve.

med.surgx.locx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.locx-step-17.caption: Bringing an infected or neoplastic specimen through the abdominal wall unprotected causes port-site infection and, in malignancy, port-site recurrence.

med.surgx.locx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.locx-step-19.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.locx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.locx-step-20.caption: A port-site hernia through an unclosed 10 mm fascial defect can strangulate, and it presents days later to someone who was not in theatre.

med.surgx.locx-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.locx-step-21.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.erx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.erx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.erx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.erx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.erx-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.erx-step-03.caption: Gynaecological and obstetric operations rest on a scan, a test result and a plan agreed in clinic.

med.surgx.erx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.erx-step-05.caption: Lithotomy with legs in supports, buttocks at the edge of the table.

med.surgx.erx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.erx-step-06.caption: The size, position and mobility of the uterus and the state of the cervix under anaesthesia decide the direction of every instrument that follows.

med.surgx.erx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.erx-step-07.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.erx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.erx-step-08.caption: Traction on the cervix straightens the canal and the cavity, and most perforations happen during sounding or dilatation of an unstraightened, unprimed cervix.

med.surgx.erx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.erx-step-09.caption: Suction removes tissue with less blood loss, fewer adhesions and less perforation risk than sharp curettage.

med.surgx.erx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.erx-step-10.caption: Retained tissue means a repeat procedure, and an evacuation that yields no pregnancy tissue may mean the pregnancy was never in the uterus.

med.surgx.erx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.erx-step-11.caption: A perforation by a sound or small dilator with no suction applied is often harmless.

med.surgx.erx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.erx-step-12.caption: Visual estimates of blood loss are consistently low.

med.surgx.erx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.erx-step-14.caption: A rhesus-negative woman exposed to fetal red cells can become sensitised, which threatens every future pregnancy.

med.surgx.erx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.erx-step-15.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.erx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.erx-step-16.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.omx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.omx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.omx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.omx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.omx-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.omx-step-03.caption: Gynaecological and obstetric operations rest on a scan, a test result and a plan agreed in clinic.

med.surgx.omx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.omx-step-05.caption: Supine, arms out, urinary catheter after vaginal preparation; slight head-down tilt once the abdomen is open.

med.surgx.omx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.omx-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.omx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.omx-step-07.caption: A transverse suprapubic incision gives good access to a pelvic organ of moderate size, with less pain and a lower risk of incisional hernia than a midline incision.

med.surgx.omx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.omx-step-08.caption: The purpose of a laparotomy is to find out.

med.surgx.omx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.omx-step-09.caption: The state of the remaining tube and both ovaries determines future fertility, the choice between salpingectomy and salpingotomy, and what the woman is told afterwards.

med.surgx.omx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.omx-step-10.caption: Myomectomy can bleed heavily and quickly.

med.surgx.omx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.omx-step-11.caption: Every uterine incision is a source of adhesions and a scar for a future pregnancy.

med.surgx.omx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.omx-step-12.caption: Staying in the pseudocapsule plane separates the fibroid from the myometrium with the least bleeding and keeps the remaining muscle intact.

med.surgx.omx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.omx-step-14.caption: Visual estimates of blood loss are consistently low.

med.surgx.omx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.omx-step-15.caption: Myomectomy bleeding can escalate faster than expected.

med.surgx.omx-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.omx-step-18.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.omx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.omx-step-19.caption: The rectus sheath is what holds the abdomen.

med.surgx.omx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.omx-step-20.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.omx-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.omx-step-21.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.wsnbx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.wsnbx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.wsnbx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.wsnbx-step-02.caption: A cancer operation is one part of a treatment plan agreed by a multidisciplinary team.

med.surgx.wsnbx-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.wsnbx-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.wsnbx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.wsnbx-step-05.caption: Supine with the ipsilateral arm abducted to no more than 90 degrees on an arm board.

med.surgx.wsnbx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.wsnbx-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.wsnbx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.wsnbx-step-08.caption: Every axillary operation, from a sentinel node biopsy to a level II clearance, starts by opening the clavipectoral fascia at the lateral border of pectoralis major.

med.surgx.wsnbx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.wsnbx-step-09.caption: The sentinel node is the first node draining the tumour.

med.surgx.wsnbx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.wsnbx-step-11.caption: The goal is clear margins with the best possible cosmetic result.

med.surgx.wsnbx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.wsnbx-step-12.caption: Margin status and nodal yield are reported by the pathologist, but only from a specimen they can orient.

med.surgx.wsnbx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.wsnbx-step-13.caption: Clips mark the tumour bed for the radiotherapy boost.

med.surgx.wsnbx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.wsnbx-step-15.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.wsnbx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.wsnbx-step-17.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.wsnbx-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.wsnbx-step-18.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.alndx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.alndx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.alndx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.alndx-step-02.caption: A cancer operation is one part of a treatment plan agreed by a multidisciplinary team.

med.surgx.alndx-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.alndx-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.alndx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.alndx-step-05.caption: Supine with the arm on an arm board abducted to no more than 90 degrees, shoulder at the edge of the table.

med.surgx.alndx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.alndx-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.alndx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.alndx-step-07.caption: A transverse or gently curved incision just below the hair-bearing skin, between pectoralis major and latissimus dorsi, gives access to all levels with a scar that is hidden by the arm and does not contract across the axilla.

med.surgx.alndx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.alndx-step-08.caption: Every axillary operation, from a sentinel node biopsy to a level II clearance, starts by opening the clavipectoral fascia at the lateral border of pectoralis major.

med.surgx.alndx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.alndx-step-10.caption: The long thoracic nerve stabilises the scapula and the thoracodorsal nerve powers latissimus dorsi.

med.surgx.alndx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.alndx-step-11.caption: Level II nodes lie behind pectoralis minor and are part of a standard clearance.

med.surgx.alndx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.alndx-step-12.caption: A lymphadenectomy stages the cancer and, in several cancers, controls regional disease.

med.surgx.alndx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.alndx-step-13.caption: The axillary and internal jugular veins form the boundaries of the commonest nodal clearances.

med.surgx.alndx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.alndx-step-14.caption: Margin status and nodal yield are reported by the pathologist, but only from a specimen they can orient.

med.surgx.alndx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.alndx-step-16.caption: A nodal clearance leaves a dead space that fills with serous fluid and lymph.

med.surgx.alndx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.alndx-step-17.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.alndx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.alndx-step-20.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.uscx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.uscx-step-10.caption: An immature tract closes quickly if the catheter falls out, and the replacement may need a second procedure.

med.surgx.uscx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.uscx-step-12.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.uulx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.uulx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.uulx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.uulx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.uulx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.uulx-step-04.caption: Lithotomy, legs in padded supports, with the ipsilateral leg lowered or the contralateral leg raised if it helps the semirigid scope align with the ureter.

med.surgx.uulx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.uulx-step-05.caption: Upper tract endourology is done by watching wires and stents you cannot see directly.

med.surgx.uulx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.uulx-step-07.caption: Every endoscopic bladder operation starts with a complete map.

med.surgx.uulx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.uulx-step-08.caption: The pyelogram shows where the obstruction is, how the ureter runs and how the calyces are arranged.

med.surgx.uulx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.uulx-step-09.caption: The safety wire is the road home.

med.surgx.uulx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.uulx-step-10.caption: An infected, obstructed kidney is a urological emergency.

med.surgx.uulx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.uulx-step-11.caption: The semirigid scope gives the best view and working channel in the distal and mid ureter, but it is a rigid rod in a mobile tube.

med.surgx.uulx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.uulx-step-12.caption: Proximal ureteric and renal stones need the flexible scope.

med.surgx.uulx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.uulx-step-13.caption: Breaking the stone is the point of the operation, but the energy that breaks stone also cuts urothelium, guidewires and scopes.

med.surgx.uulx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.uulx-step-14.caption: Residual fragments grow, cause colic and bring the patient back.

med.surgx.uulx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.uulx-step-15.caption: Ureteric injuries are graded on withdrawal, and the grade decides whether to stent, for how long, and whether imaging is needed later.

med.surgx.uulx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.uulx-step-16.caption: A stent drains an obstructed or injured ureter, but a stent in the wrong place either drains nothing or causes pain, haematuria and migration.

med.surgx.uulx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.uulx-step-17.caption: A forgotten stent encrusts, obstructs and can cost the kidney.

med.surgx.uulx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.uulx-step-19.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.uulx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.uulx-step-20.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.udsx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.udsx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.udsx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.udsx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.udsx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.udsx-step-04.caption: Lithotomy with padded supports; a flexible cystoscope in the supine patient is an alternative in some units.

med.surgx.udsx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.udsx-step-05.caption: Upper tract endourology is done by watching wires and stents you cannot see directly.

med.surgx.udsx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.udsx-step-07.caption: Every endoscopic bladder operation starts with a complete map.

med.surgx.udsx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.udsx-step-08.caption: The pyelogram shows where the obstruction is, how the ureter runs and how the calyces are arranged.

med.surgx.udsx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.udsx-step-09.caption: The safety wire is the road home.

med.surgx.udsx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.udsx-step-10.caption: An infected, obstructed kidney is a urological emergency.

med.surgx.udsx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.udsx-step-11.caption: Too short and the proximal coil drops into the ureter or the distal coil is pulled up; too long and the distal coil irritates the trigone and causes most of the stent symptoms patients complain of.

med.surgx.udsx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.udsx-step-12.caption: A stent drains an obstructed or injured ureter, but a stent in the wrong place either drains nothing or causes pain, haematuria and migration.

med.surgx.udsx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.udsx-step-13.caption: A wire that will not pass an impacted stone, an orifice that cannot be found, or a stent that will not advance all mean the same thing: further force risks perforation and sepsis, and the kidney still needs draining.

med.surgx.udsx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.udsx-step-14.caption: A double-J stent allows urine to reflux from the bladder up to the kidney.

med.surgx.udsx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.udsx-step-15.caption: A forgotten stent encrusts, obstructs and can cost the kidney.

med.surgx.udsx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.udsx-step-17.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.udsx-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.udsx-step-18.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.upx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.upx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.upx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.upx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.upx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.upx-step-04.caption: Lithotomy first for cystoscopy and ureteric catheter placement, unless a supine position allows simultaneous retrograde access.

med.surgx.upx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.upx-step-05.caption: Upper tract endourology is done by watching wires and stents you cannot see directly.

med.surgx.upx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.upx-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.urnx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.urnx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.urnx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.urnx-step-02.caption: A cancer operation is one part of a treatment plan agreed by a multidisciplinary team.

med.surgx.urnx-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.urnx-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.urnx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.urnx-step-05.caption: Laparoscopic transperitoneal: modified flank (45 to 60 degrees), operated side up, kidney rest or bridge raised under the flank, table flexed, with the arms supported and the axilla protected.

med.surgx.urnx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.urnx-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.urnx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.urnx-step-07.caption: The access decides how easily the hilum can be reached and controlled.

med.surgx.urnx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.urnx-step-08.caption: Tumour cells shed into the wound, the peritoneum or a port site produce a recurrence that no adjuvant therapy fully reverses.

med.surgx.urnx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.urnx-step-09.caption: The kidney lies behind the colon and, on each side, a different organ that can be injured: the duodenum on the right, the spleen and pancreas on the left.

med.surgx.urnx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.urnx-step-10.caption: The ureter and gonadal vein on psoas are the most reliable landmarks in the retroperitoneum.

med.surgx.urnx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.urnx-step-11.caption: The hilum is where the operation is won or lost.

med.surgx.urnx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.urnx-step-12.caption: Taking the artery first stops inflow while the vein drains the kidney; taking the vein first leaves a kidney full of blood with nowhere to go, and it bleeds.

med.surgx.urnx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.urnx-step-13.caption: Conversion is not a failure; delayed conversion is.

med.surgx.urnx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.urnx-step-14.caption: Routine adrenalectomy is not needed when imaging shows the adrenal is uninvolved; removing it adds bleeding and morbidity.

med.surgx.urnx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.urnx-step-15.caption: Bringing an infected or neoplastic specimen through the abdominal wall unprotected causes port-site infection and, in malignancy, port-site recurrence.

med.surgx.urnx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.urnx-step-16.caption: Margin status and nodal yield are reported by the pathologist, but only from a specimen they can orient.

med.surgx.urnx-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.urnx-step-18.caption: A drain tells you what is happening in a space you cannot see.

med.surgx.urnx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.urnx-step-19.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.urnx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.urnx-step-20.caption: Burst abdomen and incisional hernia are closure failures, and closure technique is one of the few variables entirely under the surgeon's control.

med.surgx.urnx-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.urnx-step-21.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.urnx-step-22.title: Step 22
med.surgx.urnx-step-22.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.uhrx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.uhrx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.uhrx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.uhrx-step-02.caption: A hydrocele, a varicocele or a 'benign' swelling can hide a testicular tumour, and the operation planned for a benign lesion is the wrong one for a cancer.

med.surgx.uhrx-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.uhrx-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.uhrx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.uhrx-step-05.caption: Supine, legs slightly apart; the penis taped up onto the abdomen out of the field.

med.surgx.uhrx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.uhrx-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.uhrx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.uhrx-step-07.caption: A transverse incision along the skin creases, between visible vessels, heals with the least scarring and bleeding; the dartos is a vascular muscle layer, and the plane beneath it determines how much the scrotum bleeds afterwards.

med.surgx.uhrx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.uhrx-step-08.caption: The choice of repair decides the dissection.

med.surgx.uhrx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.uhrx-step-09.caption: This is the first direct look at the testis and epididymis, and the last chance to recognise that the problem is not a simple hydrocele.

med.surgx.uhrx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.uhrx-step-10.caption: Removing a testicular cancer through the scrotum breaches the lymphatic drainage and may change staging and treatment.

med.surgx.uhrx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.uhrx-step-11.caption: Both repairs stop the secreting tunica vaginalis from re-forming a closed sac: Jaboulay by turning it inside out behind the testis, Lord by gathering it into a collar.

med.surgx.uhrx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.uhrx-step-13.caption: A testis replaced with a twist, or into a dead space in the scrotum, causes pain and haematoma.

med.surgx.uhrx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.uhrx-step-15.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.uhrx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.uhrx-step-17.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.uacx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.uacx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.uacx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.uacx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.uacx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.uacx-step-04.caption: Supine with the legs slightly apart.

med.surgx.uacx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.uacx-step-05.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.uacx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.uacx-step-06.caption: A good block makes the operation painless under local anaesthetic and reduces post-operative pain after a general anaesthetic.

med.surgx.uacx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.uacx-step-15.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.uacx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.uacx-step-17.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.fcs-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.fcs-step-05.caption: Supine (men) or frog-leg (women), the genitalia exposed, a screen so the patient can watch if wished.

med.surgx.vas-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.vas-step-08.caption: Sealing the cut lumen and putting a layer of fascia between the ends gives the lowest failure rate.

med.surgx.nu-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.nu-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.phx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.phx-step-16.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.pox-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.pox-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.pox-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.pox-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.pox-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.pox-step-03.caption: Infants decompensate quickly and tolerate an uncorrected metabolic, glucose or temperature problem badly.

med.surgx.pox-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.pox-step-05.caption: Infants have a large surface area for their mass and little subcutaneous fat.

med.surgx.pox-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.pox-step-06.caption: Supine, legs slightly abducted (frog-leg in an infant) so the scrotum is accessible, on a warmed mattress.

med.surgx.pox-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.pox-step-09.caption: Wound infiltration or a regional block reduces opioid need, and opioids increase the risk of post- operative apnoea in infants.

med.surgx.pox-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.pox-step-10.caption: Many palpable undescended testes lie in the superficial inguinal pouch, outside the canal.

med.surgx.pox-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.pox-step-11.caption: The gubernaculum and cremaster tether the testis.

med.surgx.pox-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.pox-step-12.caption: The patent processus is both a hernia sac and the main tether shortening the cord.

med.surgx.pox-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.pox-step-13.caption: A testis fixed under tension retracts or becomes atrophic.

med.surgx.pox-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.pox-step-14.caption: Forcing an inadequate cord into the scrotum risks losing the testis.

med.surgx.pox-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.pox-step-18.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.pox-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.pox-step-19.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.pox-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.pox-step-20.caption: Most complications of day-case genital surgery in children, such as bleeding, urinary retention and wound infection, declare themselves after the family has gone home.

med.surgx.pox-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.pox-step-21.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.pcx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.pcx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.pcx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.pcx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.pcx-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.pcx-step-03.caption: Infants decompensate quickly and tolerate an uncorrected metabolic, glucose or temperature problem badly.

med.surgx.pcx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.pcx-step-05.caption: Supine, legs slightly apart, on a warmed mattress for an infant.

med.surgx.pcx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.pcx-step-16.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.pcx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.pcx-step-17.caption: Most complications of day-case genital surgery in children, such as bleeding, urinary retention and wound infection, declare themselves after the family has gone home.

med.surgx.pcx-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.pcx-step-18.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.pirx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.pirx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.pirx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.pirx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.pirx-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.pirx-step-03.caption: Infants decompensate quickly and tolerate an uncorrected metabolic, glucose or temperature problem badly.

med.surgx.pirx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.pirx-step-04.caption: Children with intussusception or midgut volvulus are often more dehydrated and acidotic than they look, and they decompensate abruptly at induction.

med.surgx.pirx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.pirx-step-06.caption: Infants have a large surface area for their mass and little subcutaneous fat.

med.surgx.pirx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.pirx-step-07.caption: Supine on a warmed mattress, with the abdomen fully exposed and a roll under the lower chest if needed.

med.surgx.pirx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.pirx-step-08.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.pirx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.pirx-step-10.caption: Reduction is safest when it is done under direct vision with the bowel outside the wound.

med.surgx.pirx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.pirx-step-11.caption: Pushing the apex back from below spreads force over the whole wall.

med.surgx.pirx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.pirx-step-12.caption: Bowel handled roughly becomes ileus, adhesions and, at the extreme, a serosal tear that becomes a leak.

med.surgx.pirx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.pirx-step-13.caption: A missed lead point means recurrence or a missed diagnosis such as lymphoma.

med.surgx.pirx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.pirx-step-14.caption: An irreducible, perforated or gangrenous intussusception, or one with a lead point, needs resection.

med.surgx.pirx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.pirx-step-19.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.pirx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.pirx-step-20.caption: Dehiscence after a paediatric laparotomy is usually a technical failure, made more likely by distension, sepsis and poor nutrition.

med.surgx.pirx-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.pirx-step-21.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.pirx-step-22.title: Step 22
med.surgx.pirx-step-22.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.plpx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.plpx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.plpx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.plpx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.plpx-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.plpx-step-03.caption: Infants decompensate quickly and tolerate an uncorrected metabolic, glucose or temperature problem badly.

med.surgx.plpx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.plpx-step-04.caption: Children with intussusception or midgut volvulus are often more dehydrated and acidotic than they look, and they decompensate abruptly at induction.

med.surgx.plpx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.plpx-step-06.caption: Infants have a large surface area for their mass and little subcutaneous fat.

med.surgx.plpx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.plpx-step-07.caption: Supine on a warmed mattress, with a forced-air warmer and the abdomen fully exposed.

med.surgx.plpx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.plpx-step-08.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.plpx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.plpx-step-09.caption: In infants and young children the abdomen is wider than it is long.

med.surgx.plpx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.plpx-step-10.caption: The anatomy of a volvulus cannot be understood from inside the abdomen.

med.surgx.plpx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.plpx-step-11.caption: Volvulus is usually clockwise, so anticlockwise derotation, often remembered as turning back the clock, untwists it.

med.surgx.plpx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.plpx-step-13.caption: Ischaemic midgut that looks doubtful after derotation often recovers.

med.surgx.plpx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.plpx-step-19.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.plpx-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.plpx-step-21.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.plpx-step-22.title: Step 22
med.surgx.plpx-step-22.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.lsx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.lsx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.lsx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.lsx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.lsx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.lsx-step-04.caption: Supine or Lloyd-Davies with arms tucked, for Trendelenburg tilt; a uterine manipulator is optional and only if intrauterine pregnancy has been excluded.

med.surgx.lsx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.lsx-step-06.caption: Access is where laparoscopy injures people.

med.surgx.lsx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.lsx-step-08.caption: The first look answers a question the imaging could not, and it is the only chance to find the second diagnosis before attention narrows to the first.

med.surgx.lsx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.lsx-step-11.caption: The state of the remaining tube and both ovaries determines future fertility, the choice between salpingectomy and salpingotomy, and what the woman is told afterwards.

med.surgx.lsx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.lsx-step-12.caption: Bringing an infected or neoplastic specimen through the abdominal wall unprotected causes port-site infection and, in malignancy, port-site recurrence.

med.surgx.lsx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.lsx-step-14.caption: Visual estimates of blood loss are consistently low.

med.surgx.lsx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.lsx-step-15.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.bfex-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.bfex-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.bfex-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.bfex-step-02.caption: A cancer operation is one part of a treatment plan agreed by a multidisciplinary team.

med.surgx.bfex-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.bfex-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.bfex-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.bfex-step-05.caption: Supine with the ipsilateral arm abducted to no more than 90 degrees on an arm board.

med.surgx.bfex-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.bfex-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.bfex-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.bfex-step-07.caption: The scar is what the patient lives with.

med.surgx.bfex-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.bfex-step-08.caption: A fibroadenoma has a natural plane of compressed tissue around it.

med.surgx.bfex-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.bfex-step-09.caption: A small or deep lump that was palpable in clinic can be hard to feel once the patient is asleep and the breast is flattened.

med.surgx.bfex-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.bfex-step-10.caption: A small cavity fills with seroma and settles well, but a larger defect under thin skin can pull the skin inwards as it heals.

med.surgx.bfex-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.bfex-step-12.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.bfex-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.bfex-step-14.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.bfex-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.bfex-step-15.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.orrx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.orrx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.orrx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.orrx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.orrx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.orrx-step-04.caption: Supine, arms out, with a warming blanket below the waist and fluid warmers on every line.

med.surgx.orrx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.orrx-step-05.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.orrx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.orrx-step-06.caption: Loss of sympathetic tone and abdominal wall tone at induction can turn a contained rupture into a free one.

med.surgx.orrx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.orrx-step-07.caption: The midline is fast, bloodless and extensible in both directions, which is exactly what an unknown pathology needs.

med.surgx.orrx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.orrx-step-09.caption: An artery opened without control bleeds at arterial pressure into a field you can no longer see.

med.surgx.orrx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.orrx-step-10.caption: Static blood beyond a clamp clots within minutes.

med.surgx.orrx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.orrx-step-11.caption: Lumbar and inferior mesenteric back-bleeding can be heavy and continue after the main clamps are on.

med.surgx.orrx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.orrx-step-12.caption: The proximal anastomosis bears the full arterial pressure and is where most bleeding happens.

med.surgx.orrx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.orrx-step-13.caption: Clot, air and debris left in the lumen go straight to the distal bed when flow is restored.

med.surgx.orrx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.orrx-step-14.caption: Declamping releases cold, acidic, potassium-rich blood into the circulation and drops the pressure suddenly.

med.surgx.orrx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.orrx-step-15.caption: A technically perfect anastomosis with a thrombosed or embolised distal bed is a failed operation.

med.surgx.orrx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.orrx-step-17.caption: After rupture, the bowel and retroperitoneum swell and the patient is often cold, acidotic and coagulopathic.

med.surgx.orrx-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.orrx-step-18.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.orrx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.orrx-step-19.caption: Burst abdomen and incisional hernia are closure failures, and closure technique is one of the few variables entirely under the surgeon's control.

med.surgx.orrx-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.orrx-step-21.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.fex-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.fex-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.fex-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.fex-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.fex-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.fex-step-04.caption: Supine, with the whole affected leg prepped and free, and the other groin prepped for access or vein harvest.

med.surgx.fex-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.fex-step-05.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.fex-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.fex-step-06.caption: The common femoral bifurcation gives access to the iliac, superficial femoral and profunda arteries through one incision, and is where emboli most often lodge.

med.surgx.fex-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.fex-step-07.caption: An artery opened without control bleeds at arterial pressure into a field you can no longer see.

med.surgx.fex-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.fex-step-08.caption: Static blood beyond a clamp clots within minutes.

med.surgx.fex-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.fex-step-09.caption: The site and direction of the arteriotomy decide how easily the catheter enters each branch and whether the artery can be closed without narrowing.

med.surgx.fex-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.fex-step-10.caption: The balloon catheter extracts clot from vessels that cannot be reached directly.

med.surgx.fex-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.fex-step-11.caption: Clot, air and debris left in the lumen go straight to the distal bed when flow is restored.

med.surgx.fex-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.fex-step-14.caption: A technically perfect anastomosis with a thrombosed or embolised distal bed is a failed operation.

med.surgx.fex-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.fex-step-19.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.fex-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.fex-step-20.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.bkax-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.bkax-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.bkax-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.bkax-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.cex-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.cex-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.cex-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.cex-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.cex-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.cex-step-04.caption: The way you will know whether the brain tolerates clamping depends on the anaesthetic.

med.surgx.cex-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.cex-step-05.caption: Supine with the head on a ring, turned slightly away from the operative side and the neck gently extended with a roll under the shoulders.

med.surgx.cex-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.cex-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.cex-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.cex-step-09.caption: An artery opened without control bleeds at arterial pressure into a field you can no longer see.

med.surgx.cex-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.cex-step-10.caption: Static blood beyond a clamp clots within minutes.

med.surgx.cex-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.cex-step-11.caption: Most patients tolerate carotid clamping because the circle of Willis fills the hemisphere, but some do not.

med.surgx.cex-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.cex-step-12.caption: The endpoint in the internal carotid decides whether the artery stays open.

med.surgx.cex-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.cex-step-13.caption: Patch angioplasty reduces early thrombosis and restenosis compared with routine primary closure of a longitudinal arteriotomy, and ESVS recommends patch closure (or eversion) over routine primary closure.

med.surgx.cex-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.cex-step-14.caption: Clot, air and debris left in the lumen go straight to the distal bed when flow is restored.

med.surgx.cex-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.cex-step-18.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.cex-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.cex-step-20.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.cex-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.cex-step-21.caption: A new deficit after carotid endarterectomy is often due to thrombosis or a flap at the operated site, and the brain can be saved only if this is found and corrected within minutes.

med.surgx.cex-step-22.title: Step 22
med.surgx.cex-step-22.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.fpbx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.fpbx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.fpbx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.fpbx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.fpbx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.fpbx-step-04.caption: Vein operations succeed or fail on the vein.

med.surgx.fpbx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.fpbx-step-05.caption: Supine, the leg slightly externally rotated with the knee flexed on a padded support to open the medial thigh.

med.surgx.fpbx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.fpbx-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.fpbx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.fpbx-step-07.caption: The inflow anastomosis must sit on a soft segment with good pressure.

med.surgx.fpbx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.fpbx-step-08.caption: The above-knee popliteal artery lies deep to its vein in a confined space.

med.surgx.fpbx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.fpbx-step-09.caption: The long-term patency of a vein graft is largely set during harvest.

med.surgx.fpbx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.fpbx-step-12.caption: Static blood beyond a clamp clots within minutes.

med.surgx.fpbx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.fpbx-step-13.caption: An artery opened without control bleeds at arterial pressure into a field you can no longer see.

med.surgx.fpbx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.fpbx-step-14.caption: Most early graft and fistula failures are technical and sit at an anastomosis: a narrowed heel or toe, a lifted intimal flap, a purse-stringed suture line or a twisted conduit.

med.surgx.fpbx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.fpbx-step-15.caption: Clot, air and debris left in the lumen go straight to the distal bed when flow is restored.

med.surgx.fpbx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.fpbx-step-16.caption: Declamping releases cold, acidic, potassium- rich blood into the circulation and drops the pressure suddenly.

med.surgx.fpbx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.fpbx-step-17.caption: A technically perfect anastomosis with a thrombosed or embolised distal bed is a failed operation.

med.surgx.fpbx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.fpbx-step-19.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.fpbx-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.fpbx-step-21.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.afrx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.afrx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.afrx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.afrx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.afrx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.afrx-step-04.caption: Vein operations succeed or fail on the vein.

med.surgx.afrx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.afrx-step-05.caption: Small vessels in spasm are hard to sew and quick to thrombose.

med.surgx.afrx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.afrx-step-06.caption: Supine with the arm abducted on an arm table, palm up, the wrist slightly extended over a small roll.

med.surgx.afrx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.afrx-step-07.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.afrx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.afrx-step-08.caption: One incision placed between the artery and the vein reaches both without undermining, and keeps away from the superficial radial nerve branches.

med.surgx.afrx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.afrx-step-09.caption: The vein must reach the artery in a smooth curve.

med.surgx.afrx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.afrx-step-10.caption: An artery opened without control bleeds at arterial pressure into a field you can no longer see.

med.surgx.afrx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.afrx-step-11.caption: Static blood beyond a clamp clots within minutes.

med.surgx.afrx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.afrx-step-12.caption: The arteriotomy length controls the fistula flow.

med.surgx.afrx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.afrx-step-13.caption: Most early graft and fistula failures are technical and sit at an anastomosis: a narrowed heel or toe, a lifted intimal flap, a purse-stringed suture line or a twisted conduit.

med.surgx.afrx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.afrx-step-15.caption: A technically perfect anastomosis with a thrombosed or embolised distal bed is a failed operation.

med.surgx.afrx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.afrx-step-16.caption: A fistula that has only a pulse and no thrill at the end of the operation is likely to fail within hours.

med.surgx.afrx-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.afrx-step-18.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.afrx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.afrx-step-19.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.afrx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.afrx-step-20.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.gasx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.gasx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.gasx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.gasx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.gasx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.gasx-step-04.caption: Vein operations succeed or fail on the vein.

med.surgx.gasx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.gasx-step-05.caption: Supine with the leg slightly externally rotated and the knee slightly flexed.

med.surgx.gasx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.gasx-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.gasx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.gasx-step-07.caption: Cannulating at the lowest point of reflux treats the whole incompetent segment, and a single clean puncture avoids spasm and haematoma that make further attempts harder.

med.surgx.gasx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.gasx-step-08.caption: Heat delivered too close to the junction can propagate thrombus into the common femoral vein, which turns a cosmetic operation into a deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism.

med.surgx.gasx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.gasx-step-11.caption: Recurrence after open surgery comes largely from tributaries or a stump left behind, and the most serious injury in varicose vein surgery, ligation or stripping of the femoral vein, happens here.

med.surgx.gasx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.gasx-step-12.caption: Removing the refluxing thigh trunk reduces recurrence compared with junction ligation alone.

med.surgx.gasx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.gasx-step-13.caption: Treating the trunk alone often leaves visible varicosities and symptoms.

med.surgx.gasx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.gasx-step-14.caption: The serious harms of this operation come from pressing on: forcing a catheter, ablating a vein that has not been reached, or dissecting a groin whose anatomy is not understood.

med.surgx.gasx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.gasx-step-16.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.gasx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.gasx-step-17.caption: The groin is the commonest site of vascular wound complications: lymph leak, seroma, infection and breakdown over a graft or a vein stump.

med.surgx.gasx-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.gasx-step-18.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.gasx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.gasx-step-19.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.akax-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.akax-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.akax-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.akax-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.akax-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.akax-step-04.caption: Supine, with a sandbag under the ipsilateral buttock so the thigh can be lifted to reach the posterior flap.

med.surgx.akax-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.akax-step-05.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.akax-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.akax-step-06.caption: A tourniquet gives a bloodless field but adds ischaemia to injured tissue and hides bleeding that tells you what is alive.

med.surgx.akax-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.akax-step-08.caption: Dividing the anterior and medial muscles first exposes the femoral vessels in the adductor canal so they can be controlled before they are cut.

med.surgx.akax-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.akax-step-09.caption: The superficial femoral artery carries enough flow to exsanguinate a patient from a slipped tie.

med.surgx.akax-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.akax-step-10.caption: A bone end that is too long for the flaps forces a tight closure, and a sharp edge erodes through the soft tissue or makes the socket painful.

med.surgx.akax-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.akax-step-12.caption: The posterior muscles carry the perforating branches of the profunda, which bleed briskly.

med.surgx.akax-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.akax-step-13.caption: Without the adductors attached, the short femur drifts into abduction and flexion, which makes the prosthesis hard to fit and walking inefficient.

med.surgx.akax-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.akax-step-14.caption: In a septic or unstable patient, a quick circumferential amputation removes the source of sepsis in minutes; a formal stump made through infected or oedematous tissue tends to break down.

med.surgx.akax-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.akax-step-16.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.akax-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.akax-step-18.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.akax-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.akax-step-19.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.stx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.stx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.stx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.stx-step-04.caption: In ENT surgery the surgeon and the anaesthetist work in the same space.

med.surgx.stx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.stx-step-05.caption: Supine, shoulder roll, neck extended if the cervical spine allows.

med.surgx.stx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.stx-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.stx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.stx-step-11.caption: A tracheostomy tube can sit in a false passage and look perfect.

med.surgx.stx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.stx-step-12.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.stx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.stx-step-13.caption: Most ENT airway catastrophes happen after the operation, in recovery or on the ward, in the hands of people who were not in theatre.

med.surgx.stx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.stx-step-14.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.fx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.fx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.fx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.fx-step-02.caption: ENT operations are often elective and sided, and each rests on one investigation: the audiogram and tympanogram for grommets, the CT for sinus surgery, the documented infection count or sleep study for tonsillectomy.

med.surgx.fx-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.fx-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.fx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.fx-step-13.caption: A retained throat pack or a clot in the nasopharynx sitting above the larynx can obstruct the airway completely after extubation.

med.surgx.fx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.fx-step-14.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.fx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.fx-step-16.caption: Most ENT airway catastrophes happen after the operation, in recovery or on the ward, in the hands of people who were not in theatre.

med.surgx.fx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.fx-step-17.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.mgx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.mgx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.mgx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.mgx-step-02.caption: ENT operations are often elective and sided, and each rests on one investigation: the audiogram and tympanogram for grommets, the CT for sinus surgery, the documented infection count or sleep study for tonsillectomy.

med.surgx.mgx-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.mgx-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.mgx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.mgx-step-04.caption: In ENT surgery the surgeon and the anaesthetist work in the same space.

med.surgx.mgx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.mgx-step-05.caption: Supine, head turned away from the operated ear on a head ring.

med.surgx.mgx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.mgx-step-06.caption: Wax and debris hide the anatomy.

med.surgx.mgx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.mgx-step-07.caption: The anteroinferior quadrant is away from the ossicles and the chorda tympani.

med.surgx.mgx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.mgx-step-08.caption: A grommet that is not seated across the drum either extrudes early or falls into the middle ear and becomes a foreign body.

med.surgx.mgx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.mgx-step-09.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.mgx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.mgx-step-10.caption: Most ENT airway catastrophes happen after the operation, in recovery or on the ward, in the hands of people who were not in theatre.

med.surgx.mgx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.mgx-step-11.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.sx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.sx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.sx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.sx-step-02.caption: ENT operations are often elective and sided, and each rests on one investigation: the audiogram and tympanogram for grommets, the CT for sinus surgery, the documented infection count or sleep study for tonsillectomy.

med.surgx.sx-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.sx-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.sx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.sx-step-05.caption: In ENT surgery the surgeon and the anaesthetist work in the same space.

med.surgx.sx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.sx-step-06.caption: Supine with a head ring, head slightly flexed on the neck and turned a little towards the surgeon, with 15 to 20 degrees of head-up tilt.

med.surgx.sx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.sx-step-07.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.sx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.sx-step-08.caption: Nasal and ear surgery is done through a small opening under magnification, where a few drops of blood hide the plane, the nerve or the flap edge.

med.surgx.sx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.sx-step-17.caption: A retained throat pack or a clot in the nasopharynx sitting above the larynx can obstruct the airway completely after extubation.

med.surgx.sx-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.sx-step-18.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.sx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.sx-step-19.caption: Most ENT airway catastrophes happen after the operation, in recovery or on the ward, in the hands of people who were not in theatre.

med.surgx.sx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.sx-step-20.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.ax-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.ax-step-06.caption: Supine on a head ring with a shoulder roll and moderate neck extension, so the nasopharynx is visible behind the soft palate.

med.surgx.qdx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.qdx-step-14.caption: Most ENT airway catastrophes happen after the operation, in recovery or on the ward, in the hands of people who were not in theatre.

med.surgx.hhx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.hhx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.hhx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.hhx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.hhx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.hhx-step-04.caption: A deep infection around a joint replacement usually means further major surgery.

med.surgx.hhx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.hhx-step-05.caption: Lateral decubitus with pelvic supports, operated side up, with careful padding of frail skin and the down-side heel and fibular head.

med.surgx.hhx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.hhx-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.hhx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.hhx-step-07.caption: The posterior approach gives wide access to the femur and acetabulum through the gluteus maximus split and the short external rotators.

med.surgx.hhx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.hhx-step-08.caption: The level and angle of the neck cut set the starting point for leg length and offset.

med.surgx.hhx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.hhx-step-20.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.hhx-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.hhx-step-21.caption: Deficits and compartment syndrome that are found early are treatable.

med.surgx.hhx-step-22.title: Step 22
med.surgx.hhx-step-22.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.aox-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.aox-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.aox-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.aox-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.aox-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.aox-step-04.caption: Supine with a sandbag under the ipsilateral buttock to internally rotate the leg, or lateral for a posterior approach.

med.surgx.aox-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.aox-step-05.caption: A tourniquet gives a bloodless field but adds ischaemia to injured tissue and hides bleeding that tells you what is alive.

med.surgx.aox-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.aox-step-06.caption: Fixation is only as good as the images it is judged by, and every second of screening is dose to the patient and the team.

med.surgx.aox-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.aox-step-07.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.aox-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.aox-step-08.caption: The fibula is subcutaneous, so the approach is simple, but the superficial peroneal nerve crosses from posterior to anterior in the distal leg at a variable level and the skin over the fibula tolerates little retraction or a prominent plate.

med.surgx.aox-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.aox-step-09.caption: A fracture cannot be reduced accurately while clot, periosteum and soft tissue sit between the fragments.

med.surgx.aox-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.aox-step-10.caption: Fixing a malreduced fracture fixes the malreduction.

med.surgx.aox-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.aox-step-11.caption: Provisional fixation holds the reduction while it is checked in two planes and while the plate is applied.

med.surgx.aox-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.aox-step-12.caption: The wrong size, side or type cannot be undone after insertion, and an implant that is not registered cannot be traced if it is recalled.

med.surgx.aox-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.aox-step-13.caption: The plate provides the stability that lets the fracture heal and the joint move.

med.surgx.aox-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.aox-step-14.caption: A displaced medial malleolar fracture leaves the talus unstable and the joint incongruent.

med.surgx.aox-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.aox-step-15.caption: An unstable syndesmosis left unfixed lets the talus shift, but a syndesmosis fixed in a malreduced position is common and harms outcome as much.

med.surgx.aox-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.aox-step-16.caption: The final images are the evidence of what was achieved.

med.surgx.aox-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.aox-step-17.caption: Sometimes the soft tissue or the bone will not tolerate the planned fixation.

med.surgx.aox-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.aox-step-19.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.aox-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.aox-step-20.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.aox-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.aox-step-21.caption: Deficits and compartment syndrome that are found early are treatable.

med.surgx.aox-step-22.title: Step 22
med.surgx.aox-step-22.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.
