med.surgx.drfx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.drfx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.drfx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.drfx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.drfx-step-04.caption: Supine with the arm on a radiolucent hand table, forearm supinated for the volar approach.

med.surgx.drfx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.drfx-step-05.caption: A tourniquet gives a bloodless field but adds ischaemia to injured tissue and hides bleeding that tells you what is alive.

med.surgx.drfx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.drfx-step-06.caption: Fixation is only as good as the images it is judged by, and every second of screening is dose to the patient and the team.

med.surgx.drfx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.drfx-step-07.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.drfx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.drfx-step-08.caption: Working through the floor of the FCR sheath keeps the radial artery to one side and the median nerve and its palmar cutaneous branch to the other, and gives direct access to the volar radius under pronator quadratus.

med.surgx.drfx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.drfx-step-09.caption: A fracture cannot be reduced accurately while clot, periosteum and soft tissue sit between the fragments.

med.surgx.drfx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.drfx-step-10.caption: Fixing a malreduced fracture fixes the malreduction.

med.surgx.drfx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.drfx-step-12.caption: The wrong size, side or type cannot be undone after insertion, and an implant that is not registered cannot be traced if it is recalled.

med.surgx.drfx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.drfx-step-13.caption: The plate provides the stability that lets the fracture heal and the joint move.

med.surgx.drfx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.drfx-step-14.caption: Volar plates cause harm from the edges: a plate distal to the watershed line rubs the flexor tendons, and dorsal screws that are too long rupture the extensor tendons.

med.surgx.drfx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.drfx-step-16.caption: Sometimes the soft tissue or the bone will not tolerate the planned fixation.

med.surgx.drfx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.drfx-step-17.caption: The final images are the evidence of what was achieved.

med.surgx.drfx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.drfx-step-19.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.drfx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.drfx-step-20.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.drfx-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.drfx-step-21.caption: Deficits and compartment syndrome that are found early are treatable.

med.surgx.drfx-step-22.title: Step 22
med.surgx.drfx-step-22.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.arx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.arx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.arx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.arx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.arx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.arx-step-04.caption: Under anaesthesia, without guarding, the Lachman and pivot shift tests confirm the diagnosis and reveal associated laxity (collateral or posterolateral) that would change the operation.

med.surgx.arx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.arx-step-05.caption: Supine with a lateral post or leg holder, allowing hyperflexion beyond 120 degrees for the femoral tunnel.

med.surgx.arx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.arx-step-06.caption: A tourniquet gives a bloodless field but adds ischaemia to injured tissue and hides bleeding that tells you what is alive.

med.surgx.arx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.arx-step-07.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.arx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.arx-step-08.caption: Well-placed portals make every later step easier, and a systematic inspection finds the meniscal and chondral injuries that commonly accompany an ACL tear and change both the operation and the prognosis.

med.surgx.arx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.arx-step-10.caption: The graft's diameter and length decide the tunnel size and fixation.

med.surgx.arx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.arx-step-11.caption: A non-anatomical femoral tunnel, usually too high or too anterior, is a common technical cause of failure.

med.surgx.arx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.arx-step-12.caption: The tibial tunnel decides where the graft emerges in the joint.

med.surgx.arx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.arx-step-13.caption: The wrong size, side or type cannot be undone after insertion, and an implant that is not registered cannot be traced if it is recalled.

med.surgx.arx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.arx-step-14.caption: Fixation holds the graft until it incorporates.

med.surgx.arx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.arx-step-15.caption: The last look shows whether the graft impinges in extension, whether it is taut and whether the knee is now stable.

med.surgx.arx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.arx-step-16.caption: A short or amputated graft, a posterior wall blow-out or a tunnel in the wrong place each has a standard rescue.

med.surgx.arx-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.arx-step-18.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.arx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.arx-step-19.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.arx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.arx-step-20.caption: Deficits and compartment syndrome that are found early are treatable.

med.surgx.arx-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.arx-step-21.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.ssgx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.ssgx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.ssgx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.ssgx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.ssgx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.ssgx-step-04.caption: Positioned so both donor and recipient sites are accessible, with pressure areas protected.

med.surgx.ssgx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.ssgx-step-05.caption: A tourniquet gives a bloodless field but adds ischaemia to injured tissue and hides bleeding that tells you what is alive.

med.surgx.ssgx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.ssgx-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.ssgx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.ssgx-step-07.caption: Antibiotics do not reach dead tissue.

med.surgx.ssgx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.ssgx-step-09.caption: The depth of harvest decides both whether the graft takes and how well the donor heals.

med.surgx.ssgx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.ssgx-step-10.caption: Meshing lets blood and serum escape and expands the graft.

med.surgx.ssgx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.ssgx-step-11.caption: A graft takes only where it touches a vascular bed and stays still.

med.surgx.ssgx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.ssgx-step-12.caption: Photographs let the next surgeon see the wound without taking the dressing down, and they document the injury and what was done to it.

med.surgx.ssgx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.ssgx-step-13.caption: Shear and fluid collections are the commonest preventable causes of graft loss; the dressing exists to stop both.

med.surgx.ssgx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.ssgx-step-14.caption: Donor site pain often troubles patients more than the recipient site.

med.surgx.ssgx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.ssgx-step-15.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.ssgx-step-16.title: Step 16

med.surgx.cstx-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.cstx-step-03.caption: In neurosurgery the side and the level are read off a scan, not seen on the skin, and the patient often cannot confirm them.

med.surgx.cstx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.cstx-step-12.caption: The cortical entry decides what is damaged on the way to the tumour.

med.surgx.cstx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.cstx-step-13.caption: Extent of resection matters for outcome in glioma, but a new permanent deficit matters more to the patient.

med.surgx.cstx-step-17.title: Step 17

med.surgx.cstx-step-18.title: Step 18

med.surgx.cstx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.cstx-step-20.caption: The galea is the strength layer of the scalp.

med.surgx.cstx-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.cstx-step-21.caption: Post-operative haematoma and swelling present as a change in neurological observations, often hours after surgery.

med.surgx.acdf-step-14.caption: The wrong size, side or type cannot be undone after insertion, and an implant that is not registered cannot be traced if it is recalled.

med.surgx.llsx-step-14.caption: Epidural bleeding obscures the dura and roots, and blind bites in a bloody field create dural tears.

med.surgx.llsx-step-16.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.llsx-step-17.caption: The deep fascia is the barrier against CSF fistula and deep infection.

med.surgx.msx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.msx-step-04.caption: Supine with the arms tucked at the sides and padded, or abducted per unit practice, with a small roll between the scapulae to lift the sternum.

med.surgx.msx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.msx-step-06.caption: Skin landmarks are misleading in obese patients and those with asymmetric chests.

med.surgx.msx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.msx-step-07.caption: A sternotomy that wanders off the midline produces a weak, asymmetric closure and is the commonest technical root of sternal dehiscence.

med.surgx.msx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.msx-step-08.caption: In a redo the right ventricle, aorta and patent grafts may be stuck to the back of the sternum, and injury at re-entry is a major cause of death in re-operative cardiac surgery.

med.surgx.msx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.msx-step-09.caption: Gradual retraction avoids rib fractures and brachial plexus stretch, and a controlled pericardiotomy exposes the heart without injuring the innominate vein, the phrenic nerves or the heart itself.

med.surgx.msx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.msx-step-10.caption: Protamine reduces wound and mediastinal bleeding, but it can cause severe hypotension, pulmonary hypertension or anaphylaxis, and given at the wrong moment it clots the repair or the bypass circuit.

med.surgx.msx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.msx-step-12.caption: Conduction and rhythm disturbances are common after cardiac surgery, and a wire placed now is far safer than an emergency transvenous wire later.

med.surgx.msx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.msx-step-13.caption: A drain that is kinked, blocked or wrongly placed gives false reassurance while blood or air collects, and retained blood after cardiac or thoracic surgery causes tamponade, a trapped lung and empyema.

med.surgx.msx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.msx-step-14.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.msx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.msx-step-15.caption: Closing the sternum over a swollen heart or ongoing coagulopathic bleeding can cause tamponade physiology and haemodynamic collapse.

med.surgx.msx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.msx-step-17.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.msx-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.msx-step-18.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.msx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.msx-step-19.caption: After cardiac surgery, cardiac arrest is often caused by tamponade or bleeding that only opening the chest can fix, and external compressions can damage grafts and valves.

med.surgx.cx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.cx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.cx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.cx-step-04.caption: Supine with the arms tucked or, if a radial artery is harvested, the arm out on a board; roll between the scapulae.

med.surgx.cx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.cx-step-06.caption: A sternotomy that wanders off the midline produces a weak, asymmetric closure and is the commonest technical root of sternal dehiscence.

med.surgx.cx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.cx-step-07.caption: The left internal mammary artery to the left anterior descending artery is the graft most strongly linked with long-term survival.

med.surgx.cx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.cx-step-08.caption: The long-term patency of a vein graft is largely set during harvest.

med.surgx.cx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.cx-step-09.caption: Gradual retraction avoids rib fractures and brachial plexus stretch, and a controlled pericardiotomy exposes the heart without injuring the innominate vein, the phrenic nerves or the heart itself.

med.surgx.cx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.cx-step-10.caption: Cardiopulmonary bypass and cardioplegia give a still, bloodless field for the coronary anastomoses.

med.surgx.cx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.cx-step-11.caption: Most early graft and fistula failures are technical and sit at an anastomosis: a narrowed heel or toe, a lifted intimal flap, a purse-stringed suture line or a twisted conduit.

med.surgx.cx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.cx-step-12.caption: Coming off bypass is the moment the new grafts and the heart are tested.

med.surgx.cx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.cx-step-13.caption: A heart that will not come off bypass is usually telling you something specific, often a graft problem or ongoing ischaemia.

med.surgx.cx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.cx-step-14.caption: Protamine reduces wound and mediastinal bleeding, but it can cause severe hypotension, pulmonary hypertension or anaphylaxis, and given at the wrong moment it clots the repair or the bypass circuit.

med.surgx.cx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.cx-step-16.caption: Conduction and rhythm disturbances are common after cardiac surgery, and a wire placed now is far safer than an emergency transvenous wire later.

med.surgx.cx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.cx-step-17.caption: A drain that is kinked, blocked or wrongly placed gives false reassurance while blood or air collects, and retained blood after cardiac or thoracic surgery causes tamponade, a trapped lung and empyema.

med.surgx.cx-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.cx-step-18.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.cx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.cx-step-19.caption: Sternal instability leads to dehiscence and deep sternal wound infection, which carry substantial mortality.

med.surgx.cx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.cx-step-20.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.cx-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.cx-step-21.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.cx-step-22.title: Step 22
med.surgx.cx-step-22.caption: After cardiac surgery, cardiac arrest is often caused by tamponade or bleeding that only opening the chest can fix, and external compressions can damage grafts and valves.

med.surgx.avr-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.avr-step-18.caption: Sternal instability leads to dehiscence and deep sternal wound infection, which carry substantial mortality.

med.surgx.hx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.hx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.hx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.hx-step-02.caption: A cancer operation is one part of a treatment plan agreed by a multidisciplinary team.

med.surgx.hx-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.hx-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.hx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.hx-step-05.caption: Supine with a shoulder roll, neck extended on a head ring, slight reverse Trendelenburg to lower venous pressure.

med.surgx.hx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.hx-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.hx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.hx-step-07.caption: A skin-crease incision heals with a good scar, and the avascular midline between the strap muscles gives bloodless access to the thyroid bed and the parathyroids on either side.

med.surgx.hx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.hx-step-08.caption: Monitoring only helps if you know it worked at the start.

med.surgx.hx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.hx-step-09.caption: The external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve runs with or between the superior pole vessels.

med.surgx.hx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.hx-step-11.caption: Seeing the recurrent laryngeal nerve along its course is the main defence against injuring it.

med.surgx.hx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.hx-step-12.caption: A lobectomy is planned for low-risk disease.

med.surgx.hx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.hx-step-13.caption: The nerve is closest to the gland at the ligament of Berry, and small vessels here bleed.

med.surgx.hx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.hx-step-14.caption: A signal recorded after the dissection tells you whether the nerve still conducts.

med.surgx.hx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.hx-step-15.caption: Margin status and nodal yield are reported by the pathologist, but only from a specimen they can orient.

med.surgx.hx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.hx-step-17.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.hx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.hx-step-20.caption: A neck haematoma can obstruct the airway within minutes, and the people who see it first are recovery and ward staff, not the surgeon.

med.surgx.hx-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.hx-step-21.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.parathyroide-step-01.title: Step 1

med.surgx.parathyroide-step-02.title: Step 2

med.surgx.parathyroide-step-03.title: Step 3

med.surgx.parathyroide-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.parathyroide-step-05.caption: Supine, shoulder roll, neck extended on a head ring, slight reverse Trendelenburg.

med.surgx.parathyroide-step-06.title: Step 6

med.surgx.parathyroide-step-07.title: Step 7

med.surgx.parathyroide-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.parathyroide-step-08.caption: A skin-crease incision heals with a good scar, and the avascular midline between the strap muscles gives bloodless access to the thyroid bed and the parathyroids on either side.

med.surgx.hpx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.hpx-step-05.caption: Modified Lloyd-Davies with legs in padded stirrups, giving access to the anus for a transanal stapler or rectal washout and to the pelvis for a second assistant.

med.surgx.hpx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.hpx-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.hpx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.hpx-step-11.caption: The mesenteric division decides the blood supply of both cut ends.

med.surgx.hpx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.hpx-step-12.caption: The rectal stump is closed blind and left in a contaminated pelvis.

med.surgx.lpdux-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.lpdux-step-07.caption: Ports placed for the anatomy you have, rather than for the textbook, are the difference between a comfortable operation and a fight.

med.surgx.lpdux-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.lpdux-step-09.caption: The size, site and tissue quality of the perforation decide whether a laparoscopic patch is the right operation.

med.surgx.lihrx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.lihrx-step-07.caption: In TEP the whole operation happens in a space that does not exist until you make it.

med.surgx.lihrx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.lihrx-step-20.caption: A port-site hernia through an unclosed 10 mm fascial defect can strangulate, and it presents days later to someone who was not in theatre.

med.surgx.ovhrx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.ovhrx-step-13.caption: In sublay the mesh is held in place by intra-abdominal pressure against the rectus muscles, and the overlap beyond the defect, not the number of sutures, prevents recurrence.

med.surgx.lisx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.lisx-step-08.caption: Faecal incontinence is the injury of anorectal surgery and it is usually permanent.

med.surgx.lisx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.lisx-step-10.caption: The sphincterotomy is placed laterally, away from the fissure, because a posterior midline division leaves a keyhole deformity and soiling.

med.surgx.fiasx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.fiasx-step-10.caption: The decision to divide muscle is the decision about continence.

med.surgx.fiasx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.fiasx-step-13.caption: A loose seton keeps the tract draining, controls sepsis and protects the sphincter while the anatomy is defined and definitive surgery is planned.

med.surgx.lnfx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.lnfx-step-05.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.lnfx-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.lnfx-step-21.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.lsgx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.lsgx-step-06.caption: Access is where laparoscopy injures people.

med.surgx.lsgx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.lsgx-step-11.caption: Hiatal dissection is where the vagi, the pleura, the aorta and the oesophagus are injured.

med.surgx.lsgx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.lsgx-step-12.caption: Recurrent hiatal herniation is the commonest anatomical failure of antireflux and bariatric surgery.

med.surgx.lsgx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.lsgx-step-13.caption: The bougie sets the calibre of the wrap or the sleeve, and its passage is a recognised cause of oesophageal and gastric perforation.

med.surgx.lsgx-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.lsgx-step-18.caption: Bringing an infected or neoplastic specimen through the abdominal wall unprotected causes port-site infection and, in malignancy, port-site recurrence.

med.surgx.lhsx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.lhsx-step-12.caption: Where the distal line falls decides whether the operation cures the problem.

med.surgx.lhsx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.lhsx-step-15.caption: The circular stapler allows an anastomosis deep in the pelvis that cannot be sewn by hand.

med.surgx.lhsx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.lhsx-step-16.caption: A defect found on the table costs a stitch.

med.surgx.lartx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.lartx-step-12.caption: The posterior plane is the easiest to find and the one that sets up the whole dissection.

med.surgx.lartx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.lartx-step-14.caption: The distal margin and the number of stapler firings are both decided here.

med.surgx.lartx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.lartx-step-16.caption: The circular stapler allows an anastomosis deep in the pelvis that cannot be sewn by hand.

med.surgx.lartx-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.lartx-step-18.caption: A colorectal anastomotic leak is the complication that kills after this operation.

med.surgx.rhx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.rhx-step-07.caption: Upper abdominal organs sit high under the costal margin.

med.surgx.rhx-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.rhx-step-21.caption: Burst abdomen and incisional hernia are closure failures, and closure technique is one of the few variables entirely under the surgeon's control.

med.surgx.mrndx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.mrndx-step-10.caption: Clearing the posterior triangle exposes the floor of the neck.

med.surgx.dgx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.dgx-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.dgx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.dgx-step-13.caption: The left gastric artery carries the main lymphatic drainage of the lesser curve and the distal oesophagus.

med.surgx.ilox-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.ilox-step-12.caption: After an upper gastrointestinal cancer resection, oral intake may be delayed or stopped by a leak.

med.surgx.ilox-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.ilox-step-15.caption: The thoracic oesophagus is surrounded by the airway, the aorta and the thoracic duct.

med.surgx.ilox-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.ilox-step-16.caption: A lymphadenectomy stages the cancer and, in several cancers, controls regional disease.

med.surgx.utx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.utx-step-07.caption: A palpable or fixed mass suggests muscle-invasive or locally advanced disease, and this is the only moment it can be felt with the abdomen relaxed.

med.surgx.upx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.upx-step-07.caption: Every endoscopic bladder operation starts with a complete map.

med.surgx.upx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.upx-step-08.caption: The safety wire is the road home.

med.surgx.upx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.upx-step-09.caption: The pyelogram shows where the obstruction is, how the ureter runs and how the calyces are arranged.

med.surgx.upx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.upx-step-11.caption: An infected, obstructed kidney is a urological emergency.

med.surgx.upx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.upx-step-12.caption: The dilator follows the wire, and it can go further than you want it to.

med.surgx.upx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.upx-step-13.caption: Breaking the stone is the point of the operation, but the energy that breaks stone also cuts urothelium, guidewires and scopes.

med.surgx.upx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.upx-step-14.caption: Residual fragments grow, cause colic and bring the patient back.

med.surgx.upx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.upx-step-15.caption: Bleeding in PCNL is common and usually venous, and venous bleeding stops with tamponade.

med.surgx.upx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.upx-step-16.caption: A stent drains an obstructed or injured ureter, but a stent in the wrong place either drains nothing or causes pain, haematuria and migration.

med.surgx.upx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.upx-step-17.caption: How the kidney is drained at the end decides the patient's pain, the length of stay and whether a second look is easy.

med.surgx.upx-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.upx-step-18.caption: A forgotten stent encrusts, obstructs and can cost the kidney.

med.surgx.upx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.upx-step-20.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.upx-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.upx-step-21.caption: A hydrothorax or pneumothorax from a supracostal tract often shows only as falling oxygen saturation or breathlessness after the patient is turned back.

med.surgx.upx-step-22.title: Step 22
med.surgx.upx-step-22.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.uvx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.uvx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.uvx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.uvx-step-02.caption: A hydrocele, a varicocele or a 'benign' swelling can hide a testicular tumour, and the operation planned for a benign lesion is the wrong one for a cancer.

med.surgx.uvx-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.uvx-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.uvx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.uvx-step-05.caption: Supine; the operating microscope positioned before draping with a sterile cover, and the surgeon seated comfortably.

med.surgx.uvx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.uvx-step-07.caption: The subinguinal approach avoids opening the external oblique aponeurosis, which means less pain and faster recovery, at the cost of more veins and smaller arteries at this level; the microscope makes that trade worthwhile.

med.surgx.uvx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.uvx-step-08.caption: Every inguinal or subinguinal cord operation depends on lifting the whole cord cleanly into the wound.

med.surgx.uvx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.uvx-step-09.caption: The veins, artery and lymphatics lie inside the internal spermatic fascia.

med.surgx.uvx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.uvx-step-10.caption: Loss of the testicular artery can cause atrophy of the very testis the operation is meant to help.

med.surgx.uvx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.uvx-step-11.caption: Lymphatic ligation is the main cause of hydrocele after varicocelectomy.

med.surgx.uvx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.uvx-step-12.caption: Every internal spermatic vein left patent can carry reflux and cause persistence or recurrence; every artery or lymphatic caught causes harm.

med.surgx.uvx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.uvx-step-13.caption: Dilated veins outside the internal spermatic fascia can maintain the varicocele.

med.surgx.uvx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.uvx-step-14.caption: The operation is elective and for fertility or comfort; it must not cost the testis.

med.surgx.uvx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.uvx-step-16.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.uvx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.uvx-step-17.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.uvx-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.uvx-step-18.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.uiox-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.uiox-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.uiox-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.uiox-step-02.caption: A cancer operation is one part of a treatment plan agreed by a multidisciplinary team.

med.surgx.uiox-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.uiox-step-03.caption: A hydrocele, a varicocele or a 'benign' swelling can hide a testicular tumour, and the operation planned for a benign lesion is the wrong one for a cancer.

med.surgx.uiox-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.uiox-step-04.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.uiox-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.uiox-step-06.caption: Supine; the scrotum included in the field so the testis can be pushed up into the wound.

med.surgx.uiox-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.uiox-step-07.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.uiox-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.uiox-step-08.caption: The inguinal approach reaches the cord at the deep ring, where it can be controlled and ligated high, and keeps the scrotum untouched.

med.surgx.uiox-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.uiox-step-09.caption: Every inguinal or subinguinal cord operation depends on lifting the whole cord cleanly into the wound.

med.surgx.uiox-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.uiox-step-10.caption: Clamping the cord before the testis is handled closes the venous and lymphatic exit from the tumour while it is being manipulated, which is the oncological principle of the operation.

med.surgx.uiox-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.uiox-step-11.caption: Tumour cells shed into the wound, the peritoneum or a port site produce a recurrence that no adjuvant therapy fully reverses.

med.surgx.uiox-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.uiox-step-12.caption: The testis comes up into the groin wound within its coverings.

med.surgx.uiox-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.uiox-step-13.caption: Not every testicular lesion is malignant, and in a solitary testis or bilateral disease every millimetre of testis matters.

med.surgx.uiox-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.uiox-step-14.caption: The cord is the first route of spread.

med.surgx.uiox-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.uiox-step-15.caption: Many men value a prosthesis, and it is easier to place at the time of orchidectomy.

med.surgx.uiox-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.uiox-step-16.caption: Margin status and nodal yield are reported by the pathologist, but only from a specimen they can orient.

med.surgx.uiox-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.uiox-step-18.caption: The aponeurosis is the strength layer of the groin; closing it restores the canal and, done carelessly, entraps the ilioinguinal nerve in the suture line.

med.surgx.uiox-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.uiox-step-19.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.uiox-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.uiox-step-20.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.uiox-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.uiox-step-21.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-03.caption: Infants decompensate quickly and tolerate an uncorrected metabolic, glucose or temperature problem badly.

med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-05.caption: Infants have a large surface area for their mass and little subcutaneous fat.

med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-07.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-08.caption: Wound infiltration or a regional block reduces opioid need, and opioids increase the risk of post-operative apnoea in infants.

med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-09.caption: Access is where laparoscopy injures people.

med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-10.caption: Ports placed for the anatomy you have, rather than for the textbook, are the difference between a comfortable operation and a fight.

med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-11.caption: A stable, well-presented pylorus makes the myotomy controlled.

med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-12.caption: The operation relieves the obstruction by dividing every hypertrophied muscle fibre while leaving the mucosa intact.

med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-15.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-16.caption: A port-site hernia through an unclosed 10 mm fascial defect can strangulate, and it presents days later to someone who was not in theatre.

med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-17.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.phx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.phx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.phx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.phx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.phx-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.phx-step-03.caption: Infants decompensate quickly and tolerate an uncorrected metabolic, glucose or temperature problem badly.

med.surgx.phx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.phx-step-05.caption: Infants have a large surface area for their mass and little subcutaneous fat.

med.surgx.phx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.phx-step-06.caption: Supine with legs slightly apart, on a warmed mattress.

med.surgx.phx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.phx-step-08.caption: Wound infiltration or a regional block reduces opioid need, and opioids increase the risk of post-operative apnoea in infants.

med.surgx.phx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.phx-step-09.caption: In an infant the rings nearly overlie each other, so the sac can often be reached through the external ring without opening the aponeurosis, minimising dissection around the cord.

med.surgx.phx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.phx-step-11.caption: Recurrence after herniotomy is usually a residual sac.

med.surgx.phx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.phx-step-13.caption: Traction during dissection often draws the testis up into the canal.

med.surgx.phx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.phx-step-14.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.phx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.phx-step-15.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.pox-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.pox-step-07.caption: Under anaesthesia a retractile testis may come down fully, and a testis felt in clinic may become impalpable.

med.surgx.pox-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.pox-step-08.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.pox-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.pox-step-15.caption: A pouch between the scrotal skin and the dartos holds the testis in the scrotum without sutures through it.

med.surgx.pcx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.pcx-step-09.caption: The inner prepuce is adherent to the glans in young boys.

med.surgx.lsx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.lsx-step-17.caption: A port-site hernia through an unclosed 10 mm fascial defect can strangulate, and it presents days later to someone who was not in theatre.

med.surgx.locx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.locx-step-08.caption: Access is where laparoscopy injures people.

med.surgx.omx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.omx-step-13.caption: A well- closed myometrium without dead space stops bleeding, prevents an intramural haematoma, and gives the strongest possible scar for a future pregnancy.

med.surgx.wsnbx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.wsnbx-step-07.caption: A dual technique (radioisotope with blue dye, or a magnetic tracer) maximises the identification rate and lowers the false-negative rate of sentinel node biopsy.

med.surgx.wsnbx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.wsnbx-step-10.caption: Tumour cells shed into the wound, the peritoneum or a port site produce a recurrence that no adjuvant therapy fully reverses.

med.surgx.alndx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.alndx-step-09.caption: The axillary vein is the roof of a standard clearance.

med.surgx.alndx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.alndx-step-19.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.fex-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.fex-step-15.caption: Reperfusion swelling causes compartment syndrome hours later, often at night, when nerve and muscle loss are then irreversible.

med.surgx.fex-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.fex-step-17.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.bkax-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.bkax-step-04.caption: Supine, with a sandbag under the ipsilateral buttock and the knee able to flex.

med.surgx.bkax-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.bkax-step-05.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.bkax-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.bkax-step-06.caption: Most stump failures are decided at the marking: a level without enough blood supply, or flaps too short to close without tension.

med.surgx.bkax-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.bkax-step-08.caption: Named arteries in a stump must be individually suture-ligated.

med.surgx.bkax-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.bkax-step-09.caption: A sharp or prominent bone end will erode through the skin or make a prosthesis painful.

med.surgx.bkax-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.bkax-step-10.caption: A nerve cut under tension retracts away from the stump end, so the neuroma forms in protected tissue rather than where the prosthesis loads.

med.surgx.bkax-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.bkax-step-13.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.bkax-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.bkax-step-15.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.bkax-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.bkax-step-16.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.fx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.fx-step-05.caption: In ENT surgery the surgeon and the anaesthetist work in the same space.

med.surgx.fx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.fx-step-06.caption: Supine with the head of the table raised (reverse Trendelenburg) to reduce venous pressure in the nose.

med.surgx.fx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.fx-step-07.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.fx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.fx-step-08.caption: Endoscopic sinus surgery depends on the field.

med.surgx.fx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.fx-step-09.caption: The operation is functional: it restores drainage through the natural maxillary ostium.

med.surgx.fx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.fx-step-10.caption: The ethmoid labyrinth sits between the orbit and the brain.

med.surgx.fx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.fx-step-11.caption: Orbital haematoma from an anterior ethmoidal artery injury or a breach of the lamina can threaten sight within a short time.

med.surgx.tinx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.tinx-step-07.caption: The nail follows the entry point.

med.surgx.hhx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.hhx-step-09.caption: In a hemiarthroplasty the prosthetic head articulates against native cartilage.

med.surgx.hhx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.hhx-step-10.caption: The broach shapes the canal for the stem.

med.surgx.hhx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.hhx-step-11.caption: Trials are the last cheap moment to change size, offset, version or balance.

med.surgx.hhx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.hhx-step-12.caption: The wrong size, side or type cannot be undone after insertion, and an implant that is not registered cannot be traced if it is recalled.

med.surgx.hhx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.hhx-step-14.caption: The definitive implants can behave differently from the trials.

med.surgx.hhx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.hhx-step-15.caption: Fractures around a component happen during preparation, impaction or reduction, especially in osteoporotic bone.

med.surgx.hhx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.hhx-step-16.caption: Repairing the posterior capsule and rotators reduces the risk of dislocation after a posterior approach.

med.surgx.hhx-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.hhx-step-18.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.acdf-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.acdf-step-09.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.acdf-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.acdf-step-10.caption: The anterior cervical approach uses a natural plane between the carotid sheath and the visceral column.

med.surgx.acdf-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.acdf-step-11.caption: An interbody fusion fuses bone to bone through the disc space.

med.surgx.acdf-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.acdf-step-12.caption: In myelopathy and radiculopathy, the compression often lies behind the disc: osteophytes, disc fragments under or through the posterior longitudinal ligament, and uncovertebral spurs in the foramen.

med.surgx.msx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.msx-step-16.caption: Sternal instability leads to dehiscence and deep sternal wound infection, which carry substantial mortality.

med.surgx.cx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.cx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.parathyroide-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.parathyroide-step-12.caption: Whether the aim is to preserve normal parathyroids during a lobectomy or to find the abnormal one, the surgeon must recognise parathyroid tissue and know where it lives.

med.surgx.uscx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.uscx-step-13.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.uulx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.uulx-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.udsx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.udsx-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.uhrx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.uhrx-step-16.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.uacx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.uacx-step-07.caption: The prepuce may hide adhesions, smegma, lichen sclerosus, meatal stenosis or a tumour.

med.surgx.uacx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.uacx-step-08.caption: Penile cancer often presents under a phimosis.

med.surgx.uacx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.uacx-step-09.caption: The outer incision decides how much shaft skin remains.

med.surgx.uacx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.uacx-step-10.caption: Too long an inner cuff swells and looks poor; too short makes the anastomosis tight against the glans and risks injury to the sulcus.

med.surgx.uvx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.uvx-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-13.caption: A perforation repaired now is a minor event; a perforation discovered on day two is peritonitis in an infant.

med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.pyloromyotom-step-18.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.phx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.phx-step-07.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.hhx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.hhx-step-13.caption: Cement gives immediate fixation in poor bone, but pressurisation can drive marrow and fat into the circulation.

med.surgx.drfx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.drfx-step-11.caption: Provisional fixation holds the reduction while it is checked in two planes and while the plate is applied.

med.surgx.drfx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.drfx-step-15.caption: For dorsally displaced fractures that reduce closed, K-wire fixation gave similar function at one year to a volar locking plate in the DRAFFT trial, with a shorter, cheaper operation.

med.surgx.ctrx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.ctrx-step-10.caption: In the hand the nerves lie close to every structure that is released or repaired, and their position varies.

med.surgx.ctrx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.ctrx-step-12.caption: Incomplete release, usually proximally or distally, is the commonest cause of persistent symptoms.

med.surgx.ftrx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.ftrx-step-11.caption: A2 and A4 are the pulleys that matter most for flexion, but a bulky repair catching on them restricts gliding and ruptures.

med.surgx.ftrx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.ftrx-step-14.caption: In a wide-awake patient, full active movement shows what no passive test can: whether triggering has gone, or whether a repair gaps or catches on a pulley.

med.surgx.cstx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.cstx-step-09.caption: The scalp is very vascular and can lose a surprising volume of blood in a child or an anaemic adult.

med.surgx.cstx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.cstx-step-10.caption: The craniotome is safe only when its footplate is separated from the dura.

med.surgx.cstx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.cstx-step-14.caption: A brain that swells out of the craniotomy is either obstructed venous drainage, raised carbon dioxide, a new haematoma, or a lesion you have not yet dealt with.

med.surgx.dcx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.dcx-step-09.caption: The temporalis covers the temporal squama, which has to be removed to decompress the temporal lobe.

med.surgx.dcx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.dcx-step-11.caption: Uncal herniation compresses the brainstem from the temporal lobe.

med.surgx.dcx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.dcx-step-14.caption: A brain that swells out of the craniotomy is either obstructed venous drainage, raised carbon dioxide, a new haematoma, or a lesion you have not yet dealt with.

med.surgx.dcx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.dcx-step-19.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.dcx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.dcx-step-20.caption: The galea is the strength layer of the scalp.

med.surgx.llsx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.llsx-step-12.caption: Iatrogenic instability is a recognised late failure of decompression.

med.surgx.plftx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.plftx-step-14.caption: An interbody fusion fuses bone to bone through the disc space.

med.surgx.plftx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.plftx-step-16.caption: Rods connect the screws into a construct.

med.surgx.vbpx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.vbpx-step-05.caption: Lateral decubitus with the operated side up, an axillary roll below the dependent axilla, and the table broken to open the intercostal spaces.

med.surgx.vbpx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.vbpx-step-07.caption: The first port enters a chest that may contain adherent lung, and a low port can enter the abdomen.

med.surgx.vbpx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.vbpx-step-14.caption: A drain that is kinked, blocked or wrongly placed gives false reassurance while blood or air collects, and retained blood after cardiac or thoracic surgery causes tamponade, a trapped lung and empyema.

med.surgx.msx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.msx-step-05.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.hx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.hx-step-10.caption: Whether the aim is to preserve normal parathyroids during a lobectomy or to find the abnormal one, the surgeon must recognise parathyroid tissue and know where it lives.

med.surgx.fiasx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.fiasx-step-09.caption: A fistula is cured only when the internal opening is dealt with.

med.surgx.oscx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.oscx-step-07.caption: In a severely inflamed field the landmarks are hidden.

med.surgx.oscx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.oscx-step-13.caption: Occluding the hepatoduodenal ligament stops hepatic arterial and portal inflow.

med.surgx.bkax-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.bkax-step-11.caption: The posterior flap carries the best blood supply and the muscle padding for the stump.

med.surgx.cex-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.cex-step-07.caption: A good exposure lets you control the internal carotid beyond the plaque without traction on the bulb or the nerves.

med.surgx.cex-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.cex-step-08.caption: Cranial nerve injury is the commonest complication of carotid surgery.

med.surgx.cex-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.cex-step-15.caption: Declamping releases cold, acidic, potassium-rich blood into the circulation and drops the pressure suddenly.

med.surgx.cex-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.cex-step-16.caption: Protamine reduces wound and mediastinal bleeding, but it can cause severe hypotension, pulmonary hypertension or anaphylaxis, and given at the wrong moment it clots the repair or the bypass circuit.

med.surgx.fpbx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.fpbx-step-10.caption: A small, sclerosed or diseased vein used because it was already harvested is a common cause of early failure.

med.surgx.fpbx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.fpbx-step-11.caption: A twisted, kinked or compressed graft thromboses regardless of how good the anastomoses are.

med.surgx.fpbx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.fpbx-step-20.caption: The groin is the commonest site of vascular wound complications: lymph leak, seroma, infection and breakdown over a graft or a vein stump.

med.surgx.fpbx-step-22.title: Step 22
med.surgx.fpbx-step-22.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.afrx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.afrx-step-14.caption: Declamping releases cold, acidic, potassium-rich blood into the circulation and drops the pressure suddenly.

med.surgx.gasx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.gasx-step-09.caption: Tumescent fluid provides analgesia, compresses the vein onto the catheter for effective heat transfer, and creates a heat sink that protects the skin and nerves.

med.surgx.gasx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.gasx-step-10.caption: Ablation closes the refluxing vein permanently only when the right energy is delivered along its length; checking the deep vein afterwards finds the thrombus that would otherwise present as a pulmonary embolism.

med.surgx.akax-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.akax-step-07.caption: A stump that cannot be closed without tension will break down.

med.surgx.stx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.stx-step-07.caption: The midline raphe between the strap muscles is the avascular corridor to the trachea.

med.surgx.stx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.stx-step-08.caption: The isthmus lies over the rings where the window will be.

med.surgx.stx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.stx-step-10.caption: This is the moment the airway changes hands.

med.surgx.sx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.sx-step-09.caption: The incision decides which part of the septum you can correct.

med.surgx.sx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.sx-step-10.caption: The subperichondrial plane is avascular and strong.

med.surgx.sx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.sx-step-11.caption: Most deviations involve both cartilage and bone.

med.surgx.sx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.sx-step-12.caption: Only the deviated segment needs to go.

med.surgx.sx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.sx-step-13.caption: A basal spur or a cartilage edge dislocated off the maxillary crest is the commonest cause of persisting obstruction, and the commonest site of a flap tear.

med.surgx.sx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.sx-step-14.caption: A tear on one side heals.

med.surgx.sx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.sx-step-15.caption: The space between the flaps fills with blood if it is left open.

med.surgx.tux-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.tux-step-06.caption: Supine with the head turned away from the operative ear on a head ring, with head-up tilt.

med.surgx.lfx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.lfx-step-07.caption: Incisions placed on the fasciotomy lines decompress the compartments and preserve the perforators on which later local flaps depend.

med.surgx.pcx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.pcx-step-07.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.pirx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.pirx-step-09.caption: In infants and young children the abdomen is wider than it is long.

med.surgx.pirx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.pirx-step-15.caption: A handsewn anastomosis adapts to bowel of mismatched calibre, to thick oedematous wall and to settings without a stapler.

med.surgx.pirx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.pirx-step-16.caption: After a Ladd procedure the caecum lies in the left upper abdomen, so later appendicitis presents in the wrong place.

med.surgx.plpx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.plpx-step-12.caption: Bowel handled roughly becomes ileus, adhesions and, at the extreme, a serosal tear that becomes a leak.

med.surgx.plpx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.plpx-step-14.caption: Ladd bands compress the duodenum; dividing them relieves the extrinsic obstruction.

med.surgx.plpx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.plpx-step-15.caption: Volvulus happens because the mesenteric base is narrow.

med.surgx.plpx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.plpx-step-16.caption: After a Ladd procedure the caecum lies in the left upper abdomen, so later appendicitis presents in the wrong place.

med.surgx.plpx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.plpx-step-20.caption: Dehiscence after a paediatric laparotomy is usually a technical failure, made more likely by distension, sepsis and poor nutrition.

med.surgx.lsx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.lsx-step-05.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.lsx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.lsx-step-07.caption: Ports placed for the anatomy you have, rather than for the textbook, are the difference between a comfortable operation and a fight.

med.surgx.lsx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.lsx-step-09.caption: In a ruptured ectopic the bleeding source is small and accessible.

med.surgx.lsx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.lsx-step-10.caption: Removing the tube with its pregnancy is definitive and avoids persistent trophoblast.
